title: allow setting another devfs ruleset
body:
Hi,

Thanks for the amazing tool podman.
I'm using it on FreeBSD and after an hour of debugging the devfs mount ruleset I found that the ruleset was hardcoded to 4.
That happens on this line:
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/eeeb322d33186b6fdb8522de61ac442c0ae7de81/pkg/specgen/generate/oci_freebsd.go#L95

Would it be an idea to make the ruleset a variable that the operator can set? With a default of 4.

comments.body:
Hi, I'd like to work on this. If I read oci_freebsd.go correctly, the ruleset is only used
for the Linux-emulation devfs mount, next to the hardcoded "rule=path shm unhide".
I'd keep 4 as the default. Which would you prefer for setting it: a containers.conf option
(needs a change in containers/common), an annotation, or a podman run flag?
I can't run FreeBSD locally, so I'd add a unit test for the option building and
cross-compile for GOOS=freebsd. Would that be acceptable?

please follow our issue template, i.e. feature request, in the future.

I cant speak to freebsd at all, that is maintained by @dfr

If you need to expose a device or devices to a container, you can use Podman's `--device` option. This uses the hard-coded ruleset 4 as a base and modifies the container's devfs instance to expose the selected device nodes. For FreeBSD-native containers, the ruleset choice happens in the runtime-tools package [here](https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-tools/blob/master/generate/generate.go#L251).

I'm not opposed to making the ruleset variable but first, I would like to understand why `--device`  is not enough for your use-case.

I tried --device /dev/bpf to enable the use of a dhcp client. Maybe I don't understand it correctly, but I also seem to need --device /dev/bpf0, but this is a symlink which was not exposed to the jail afterwards.
So I couldn't get it to work with --device.
After adding `add path 'bpf*' unhide` to "devfsrules_jail=4" it worked. But I don't like changing global defaults for only a specific container. That is how I came to asking for having devfs_ruleset as an option.

I'm also open for other solutions to my bpf problem.

Thanks for the clarification - it might be possible to fix `--device` to accept the wildcard. In the meantime you could try `--privileged` which mounts the full devfs into the container, just for experimentation.

EDIT: I did some testing with `ocijail` and if we can get Podman to accept `/dev/bpf*` as a valid device name and pass it down to `ocijail`, then it does unhide both `bpf` and the `bpf0` symlink.

@dfr sir @ronaldklop sir Would it make more sense to handle this in `--device` by supporting wildcard paths on FreeBSD? From the discussion, `/dev/bpf*` seems to be the main use case, and supporting that might solve the problem without adding another configuration option for the devfs ruleset.

I’d be happy to look into the existing device handling and see whether wildcard support can be added without changing the current behaviour. Does that sound like a reasonable direction?

> I did some testing with ocijail and if we can get Podman to accept /dev/bpf* as a valid device name and pass it down to ocijail, then it does unhide both bpf and the bpf0 symlink

The spec and podman expects real paths in the config, wildcard expansion is not part of the spec, `*` is in theory a valid path name so we cannot assign a special meaning to that all of the sudden.

In a typical FreeBSD /dev, there are two bpf-related nodes, `/dev/bpf' which is the actual device node and `/dev/bpf0` which is a symbolic link to `/dev/bpf`.
 
Part of the problem here is that attempts to expose `/dev/bpf0` are silently ignored somewhere in Podman:

```
# podman run -ti --device /dev/bpf --device /dev/bpf0 --rm ghcr.io/freebsd/freebsd-notoolchain:15.0 ls -l /dev
total 1
crw-------  1 root wheel     0x25 Oct 22 13:02 bpf
crw-rw-rw-  1 root wheel    0x25f Oct 22 13:03 crypto
dr-xr-xr-x  2 root wheel      512 Oct 22 13:02 fd
crw-rw-rw-  1 root wheel     0x15 Oct 29 14:41 null
crw-rw-rw-  1 root wheel    0x234 Oct 22 13:03 ptmx
dr-xr-xr-x  2 root wheel      512 Oct 29 14:41 pts
crw-r--r--  1 root wheel      0x5 Oct 22 13:03 random
lrwxr-xr-x  1 root wheel        4 Oct 29 14:41 stderr -> fd/2
lrwxr-xr-x  1 root wheel        4 Oct 29 14:41 stdin -> fd/0
lrwxr-xr-x  1 root wheel        4 Oct 29 14:41 stdout -> fd/1
lrwxr-xr-x  1 root wheel        6 Oct 29 14:41 urandom -> random
crw-rw-rw-  1 root wheel     0x16 Oct 22 13:02 zero
crw-rw-rw-  1 root operator  0x4c Oct 22 13:02 zfs
```

This seems like a logic problem in the FreeBSD device handling code path in Podman. Perhaps a fix might be to just allow symbolic links as well as devices.

> This seems like a logic problem in the FreeBSD device handling code path in Podman. Perhaps a fix might be to just allow symbolic links as well as devices.

Yes I guess that is the actual problem, the device option seem to resolve the symlink first and does not expose the device at the given path which seem unexpected if not wrong. Would be nice to double check what docker does in that case.

I do see the resolving quite clearly here:
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/f2432e48c7eda9e0f0202e18069400d886d157e0/pkg/specgen/generate/config_linux.go#L46-L51

And following the history for a while that seems to be added first here 1ad6f9af1552cbe2119af6cda83db5b3908556db which does not say why the code needs to resolve the path, I mean if we want to walk the directory sure we follow the link in that case but for a single device that makes no sense.
Technically changing the behavior could qualify as breaking change and if we would not resolve the symlink it means we will not recreate the symlink as is either but rather create the same device at the given path directly. 

cc @giuseppe @mheon WDYT?

The concern was almost certainly related to privileged containers, but I cannot recall exact details...

This seems like it could be justified as a bugfix to me, the current behavior seems to be breaking user expectations. I am concerned about potentially breaking something, though, our testing around devices and privileged containers is perfunctory at best.
